verses.1: And famine has come upon the land.
verses.2: And when they had eaten the food that they brought from Egypt, he said to them, “Our ancestors returned to us with some food.”
verses.3: And Yehuda said to him, “The judge has given us orders that we must not see his face.”
verses.4: If you send our brothers to us, then we will come and serve you.
verses.5: And if you do not send them, then we will not go down. For the man said to us, “Do not see my face, for I am not with you.”
verses.6: And Israel said, “Why do you want me to tell that man who is your brother?”
verses.7: And Shaul said to him, “The man asked us and our descendants, saying, ‘Your ancestors had a brother. But if you refuse to do this, then know that he will say, ‘Take away your brother.’”
verses.8: And Yehuda said to Israel, “Your father sent me away. Let us go and take revenge. Let us live, and not die. Neither we nor you will die.”
verses.9: I will ask you directly if you don’t bring it to me and show it before you. My sins have been shown to you all these days.
verses.10: For if not, then it seems like we have just returned to that time when everything was in chaos.
verses.11: And Israel’s father said to them, “If that is true, then let them take some of the produce from the land with them. They should give as a offering to each man a little grain, along with some meat and vegetables.”
verses.12: And take back the money that has been taken from you. The money that has been stolen from your mouths, you must keep it in your hands. Otherwise, it will be lost.
verses.13: And they took our brothers and went back to that man again.
verses.14: And He will show you mercy before that man. He will send you another brother, along with his sons. And I have done as I promised.
verses.15: And those men took this offering and the silver coins. They carried them with them. Then they got up and went down from Egypt. They stood before Joseph.
verses.16: And Joseph saw them with their children. He said to those who were in his house, “Bring the people out into the field. They will eat there.”
verses.17: And the man did as Joseph said. He brought the men into Joseph’s house.
verses.18: And the people became afraid, because they came to Joseph’s house. They said, “Regarding the money that was taken from us at the beginning, we are here to complain about it. We want to be freed from this situation, and we want to be taken as slaves again.”
verses.19: And they went to the man who lived in the house of Joseph. They spoke to him at the entrance of the house.
verses.20: And they said to me, “Lord, let us descend down from the beginning, so that we may destroy the food supply.”
verses.21: And when we arrived at the treasury, our bags were opened. And there was gold in each bag, in its own weight. We took it into our hands.
verses.22: And another amount of money was brought to us in our hands. It wasn’t known who had put that money in our bags during our journey.
verses.23: And Shalom said to you, “Do not fear your gods. Your ancestors gave you the Torah as a gift. They brought it to me, and I revealed its name to them.”
verses.24: And the man brought the people to Joseph’s house. He gave them water to wash their feet, and he also provided food for their meals.
verses.25: They prepared the meal for Yosef’s arrival in the evening, because they heard that there they would eat bread.
verses.26: And Joseph entered the house. The women brought him the offerings that they had with them. They bowed down to him on the ground.
verses.27: And he asked them for forgiveness. He said, “Forgive your father, who is old. You said that he would be alive again.”
verses.28: And they said, “May Shalom be with you, O servant of our Father. May He still live in us.” And they bowed their heads in reverence.
verses.29: And he raised his eyes and saw his younger brother, Benjamin. He said, “This is our brother, the little one, whom you mentioned to me.” And God said, “May your son be blessed.”
verses.30: And Joseph rushed to his brothers, as his mercy had been revealed to him. He tried to kiss them. Then he entered the courtyard and kissed them.
verses.31: And he washed his face, then went out and stood there. He said, “Let them be destroyed!”
verses.32: And they gave it to him alone, and to them alone. And to the Egyptians, who ate it alone. For the Egyptians were unable to eat the grains as bread, because it was too difficult for them to digest.
verses.33: And they sat down before him, the old man in his old state, and the young man in his youthful state. And the people stood up, one by one, to face him.
verses.34: And he raised his hands from his face towards them. Then, Benyamin’s hands also rose from their positions. In total, there were five hands that rose. They drank, and they were satisfied with it.
